name: RDL Core Box Demo
subtitle: Mire Core Training Scenario | Built for one RDL Core box
description: A 3-round beginner teaching game built from a single RDL Core box: 366 vs 366 points, two Mire-core M.A.P.s and one Hyena missile drone per side. Red plays a long-range fire-support style while Blue plays a tougher bulwark/missile style. It teaches timing dials, stances, movement, Command Phase drones, MC-3 Razor missiles, delayed projectiles, objectives, and terrain lanes.

blue.name: RDL Blue Team - Bulwark / Missile Pressure

scoring.name: Centre presence
scoring.note: At End Phase if you have at least one M.A.P. on or adjacent to F7 or G6.

scoring.name: Relay pressure
scoring.note: At End Phase if you have at least one M.A.P. on or adjacent to any relay marker.

scoring.name: Projectile lesson
scoring.note: First time one of your projectiles damages an enemy. A drone missile can also score Drone lesson if it qualifies.

scoring.name: Drone lesson
scoring.note: First time your drone damages an enemy with a missile. Can be scored at the same time as Projectile lesson.

scoring.name: Part destruction
scoring.note: First time you destroy an enemy M.A.P. part during the game.

scoring.name: Drone kill
scoring.note: If you destroy the enemy Hyena Missile drone.

simplifications: Ignore full smoke complexity
Ignore Intercept / anti-missile rules (AMS-190 has Intercept 3 but is not used in the first run)
Ignore Optical Camouflage and Low Profile
Ignore advanced electronic warfare
Ignore full mission/tactics cards
Ignore surplus damage edge cases
Each drone may launch at most 2 missiles total during the 3-round demo
The Blue Missile / Brawler M.A.P. may launch at most 2 missiles total during the demo
Resolve one missile at a time and announce the target before rolling
notes: Round 1 scripted: everyone picks Movement (Blue Missile/Brawler may pick Projectile); mechs advance to the D/E and I/H columns using centre terrain as cover; drones may launch or reposition; missiles resolve in Delay Phase.
Round 2 semi-scripted: Red Fire Support = Firing, Blue Bulwark = Firing (DEF stance if exposed), missile units = Projectile or Movement; Round 3 is free play, then swap sides and replay.
Part targeting shortcut: roll a D6 - 1 Torso, 2 Chassis, 3 Left Arm, 4 Right Arm, 5 Backpack, 6 attacker chooses.
Wall and container orientations are not printed in the booklet; vertical tall walls / horizontal short walls and containers were inferred from map symmetry.
R-20 Railgun is listed as Left Arm and AC-150 HMG as Right Arm in the booklet, matching cards 032 and 030.

name: Asymmetric Duel Demo
subtitle: Twin Mire Hunters vs UN Elite | RDL two-M.A.P. team vs UN elite M.A.P. + drone
description: A 3-round asymmetric teaching game: two lighter RDL M.A.P.s (351 pts) against one elite UN M.A.P. plus a Porcupine CIWS drone (351 pts). RDL wins by splitting, scoring relays, and surviving; UN wins by holding the centre and threatening decisive damage. Teaches activation economy, elite unit pressure, missiles, Simple Intercept, repair, and objective play.

name: Signal Relay War Demo
subtitle: Electronic Warfare and Command Network Scenario | RDL Signal Net vs UN Drone Interference Cell
description: A 4-round intermediate teaching game about the information war: RDL (455 pts, two M.A.P.s plus a Hyena drone) builds a signal net of relays, Terminals, and Uplinks, while UN (454 pts, one elite command M.A.P. plus four drones) jams and disrupts it. Victory comes from relay control, Terminal access, electronic counter-rolls, command efficiency, and drone play rather than raw damage.

Teaches launch/path/impact grid thinking, Interception Tokens, saturation fire, Fire in arc, and escort decisions.

name: Power Spike
subtitle: Ammo and Charge Timing Demo Scenario
description: A 4-round intermediate/advanced scenario about resource timing: charging, conserving ammo, holding Link, and committing to one decisive turn. RDL fields a two-M.A.P. capacitor strike pair (411 pts) against a UN burst assault ace with drone support (412 pts) on a map of Reactor Relays, Ammo Caches, and Core Nodes. Players score for preparing, threatening, baiting, and committing at the right time, not just for damage.

subtitle: Melee Lock, Forced Movement, Facing, and Choke-Point Control | RDL Breach Team vs UN Gate Guard
description: A 4-round intermediate/advanced close-quarters scenario: an RDL breach pair (423 pts) must force a path through a fortified centre gate held by a UN gate guard (424 pts). It teaches Melee Lock, facing, forced movement (Push, Knock Back, Drag), screening/body-blocking, and scoring by moving through defended space rather than destroying parts.

name: Hold Until Extraction
subtitle: Damage Control Demo Scenario
description: A 4-round intermediate damage-control scenario: an RDL team (372 pts) escorts a pre-damaged data-carrier M.A.P. toward an eastern extraction zone while a UN pursuit team (381 pts) tries to disable its key parts before it escapes. Teaches part targeting, damaged/destroyed parts, Repaired Tokens, Stabilize System, Link restoration, and survival decisions.

units.name: Damaged Data Carrier M.A.P.
units.pointsNote: R-20 Shoulder-Mounted Railgun side not stated; right-hand card 033 chosen because the Type 77 Bulwark is left-hand. Starts with damaged Chassis, Link 1 lower than normal, and the Data Core scenario marker attached.

scoring.name: Successful extraction

scoring.name: Carrier survives

scoring.name: Disable mobility

scoring.name: Disable mission systems

simplifications: Ignore full stealth, full electronic warfare, full mission/tactics cards, and advanced campaign rules unless players request them
Part targeting shortcut while learning: roll a D6 - 1 Torso, 2 Chassis, 3 Left Arm, 4 Right Arm, 5 Backpack, 6 attacker chooses
notes: Sides mapped: RDL = red (escort side), UN = blue (pursuit side). Note the deployment is unusual: RDL starts at B6/B8 and extracts eastward into K5-K8, so both forces are on the same half at the start.
Starting damage setup: Carrier Chassis is Damaged at game start, Carrier Link starts 1 lower than normal, and the Data Core scenario marker is attached to the carrier.
Marker kinds follow the booklet's terminology: 'extraction' = Extraction Zone K5-K8, 'relay' = Repair Relays (F6, G7), 'datacache' = optional Data Cache scoring/pressure spaces (F7, G6).
The booklet describes a centre 'blocked by wreckage and walls' but lists no terrain grids, so terrain was left empty - dress the centre freely.
UN board setup allows 'the listed Raven-style support drone or another approved UN support drone of similar value' (30 pts) at J9.

Round 1 scripted: carrier moves toward D6/F6 with cover; escort screens; UN Hunter takes the upper lane, support covers the lower lane. Rounds 3-4: extraction race. Optional replays: full part targeting, persistent critical damage, extraction timer, emergency tow.

Support drone substitution: the booklet lists a "Raven-style support drone / approved UN support drone" at 30 pts and explicitly permits another approved UN support drone of similar value. Card 161 ADK15/MAS "Porcupine" Microwave Type is used here, matching 30 pts exactly; the booklet setup row itself reads "UN Porcupine / Raven Drone".

name: Full Game Setup Guide - Core vs Core
subtitle: Core Box vs Core Box Standard 1v1 | RDL vs UN
description: Not a scripted scenario but a full setup guide for a first unscripted standard game: force-building by role, part-slot and pilot advice, a faction cheat sheet, a 450-point / 5-round recommended format, the generic 'Relay Control' mission, and a neutral board layout. It includes a sample core-box vs core-box force pair (RDL 449 pts vs UN 447 pts) which is loaded here as the playable content.

scoring.name: Centre control
scoring.note: At End Phase, at least one M.A.P. on or adjacent to F7 or G6.

scoring.name: Relay pressure
scoring.note: At End Phase, at least one M.A.P. on or adjacent to any relay marker.

scoring.name: Wide relay control
scoring.note: At End Phase, you control a relay on both the upper half and lower half of the board.

scoring.name: First part destroyed
scoring.note: First time you destroy an enemy M.A.P. part.

scoring.name: Drone neutralised
scoring.note: Destroy or remove an enemy drone.

scoring.name: Endurance
scoring.note: At the end of Round 5, if both of your M.A.P.s are still on the board.

simplifications: Recommended first standard game: 450 points, 5 rounds, two M.A.P.s plus 0-2 drones/support pieces per side
Use standard attacks, movement, stances, Link, drones, projectiles, terrain protection; add stealth/EW/Intercept only if both players know them
Beginner control wording: a M.A.P. controls a space if it is on or adjacent to it and no enemy M.A.P. is also on or adjacent to it; drones contest only if both players agree
notes: This booklet is primarily a force-building and setup walkthrough (roles, part slots, pilots, faction cheat sheets, a complexity ladder, and a blank worksheet); the units loaded here are its 'sample core-box vs core-box force pair'.

The guide gives deployment zones (RDL columns A-B, UN columns K-L) but no exact starting grids; unit grids A5/A8/B6/B7 and L5/L8/K7 were assigned following the convention used by every other booklet in the series - treat them as suggestions.
Round flow: Command, Planning, Action, Automatic, Delay, End Phase each round; mission is the generic 'Relay Control'.
Pilot mapping: 'Rifleman-27' = card LPA-27 'Rifleman1' (9 pts), 'Charger-31' = card LPA-31 'Charger1' (6 pts); points match the guide.
Wall/container orientations inferred from map symmetry (not printed in the guide).
All sample-list arm sides are printed explicitly - R-20 (L), AC-150 (R), Shield+Cleaver (L), AC-32 (R), S100+Grenade Pod (L), R33 (R), S9 Meteor+M5 Pile Bunker (L), R7 (R) - and all match card slots.
